title: Min Stack
statement:
Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.

Implement the `MinStack` class:
- `MinStack()` initializes the stack object.
- `void push(int val)` pushes the element `val` onto the stack.
- `void pop()` removes the element on the top of the stack.
- `int top()` gets the top element of the stack.
- `int getMin()` retrieves the minimum element in the stack.

You must implement a solution with `O(1)` time complexity for each function.

Input format: Number of operations, then each operation on a new line (push val / pop / top / getMin).
constraints:
- `-2^31 <= val <= 2^31 - 1`
- Methods `pop`, `top` and `getMin` operations will always be called on non-empty stacks.
- At most `3 * 10^4` calls will be made to `push`, `pop`, `top`, and `getMin`.
hints: Use an auxiliary stack to track minimums.
Push current min to aux stack whenever pushing, pop from both on pop.

title: Minimum Stack with O(1) Min
statement:
Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element, all in O(1) time.

Process `q` operations:
- `push x` — Push x
- `pop` — Remove top
- `top` — Print top element
- `min` — Print current minimum

Assume the stack is never empty when `pop`, `top`, or `min` is called.
hints: Maintain two stacks: one main and one for minimums.
Push to min-stack only when new element <= current min.

title: Score of Parentheses
statement:
Given a balanced parentheses string `s`, compute its score:
- `()` has score 1
- `AB` has score A + B
- `(A)` has score 2*A
constraints:
- `2 <= s.length <= 50`
- `s` is a balanced parentheses string.
hints: Use a stack starting with [0].
On `(`, push 0.
On `)`, pop v; if v==0, top+=1; else top += 2*v.
